full_judgment: 2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, is short, are that the respondent herein as writ petitioner filed the Writ. Petition No. 3131 of 1991 before the High Court Division challenging the judgment and order dated 30.10.1991 passed by the Court of Settlement, Dhaka in Case No. 492 of 1987 purporting to declare the writ petitioner's House being Holding No. 59, Gour Nitai Shaha Street, Banogram Road, within Police Station Sutrapur, Dhaka as an abandoned property at the face of the writ petitioner's claim of ownership and possession from West Bangal (India), she along with her husband Amir Hossain, her children and her brother Abdul Aziz came to the then Province of East Pakistan in the year 1950 and thereafter, they took shelter at holding No.3, Taker Hat Lane, Banogram and that they acquired citizen-ship of Bangladesh by operation of law having resided permanently in Bangladesh and that in course of their stay, Abdul Aziz, her brother, acquired the case property, which belonged to Mrs. Solak Dhamini Banik, by way of exchange of his property in India with the case property and the deed of exchange having been registered after complying all legal formalities the said Abdul Aziz took possession of the case property and started living there-in with the writ petitioner along with her husband and children. The said Abdul Aziz got his name mutated in the record of right in respect of the case property; the writ petitioner, being the full sister of the aforesaid Abdul Aziz, purchased the case property from him by a registered deed of sale dated 03.06.77 at a consideration of Taka 45,000/- and after purchase she got her name mutated and paid rent to the Government and also paid taxes to the Municipality and while being in possession of the case property, she suddenly received the notice dated 17.11.1985 by which the Sectional Head of the Office of Abandoned Properties, Ministry of Works asked her to appear before him personally and to show to him all the documents of her title over the case property. She, being a pardanishin lady, complied with the said notice by sending her husband, Md. Amir Hossain, to the Sectional Head and said Md. Amir Hossain showed to Sectional Head all the deeds and documents and thereafter, the write petitioner received no further notice or any intimation from the said Office of Abandoned Properties and/or any quarter. But, surprisingly the Government listed the suit property as an abandoned property. The Government, though appeared in the above case, did not file any written statement, but, even then the Court of Settlement dismissed the above case. Hence, the writ petitioner finding no other alternative efficacious remedy filed the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule Nisi.
